question: Why does opening more checkouts at a supermarket only help if any cashier can serve any customer?
options: A customer who must return to the same cashier cannot be sent to a free checkout
Cashiers need the same colour uniform
More checkouts always cost less than faster cashiers
explanation: This is stateless scaling. If each server must keep the user's data in its own memory, the balancer cannot send the user anywhere else, and extra servers do not help that user.
